facts.text: SEO is search engine optimization. AEO is the same job for answer engines: be the page the answer comes from.
AEO tip: put the answer in the first sentence under the question. Machines and people both skim.
llms.txt is a plain-text brief of your site, written for AI tools. This site has one.
robots.txt has been around since 1994. It is still the first file a crawler asks for.
Structured data (JSON-LD) tells search engines what a page is in a format machines read directly.
FAQ schema marks up questions and answers so machines can read them. The page still has to be good.
Core Web Vitals measure loading (LCP), responsiveness (INP) and layout stability (CLS).
INP replaced FID as a Core Web Vital in March 2024. It looks at every interaction, not just the first.
CLS is the page jumping while it loads. Reserve space for images and it mostly goes away.
Shopify started in the mid-2000s when its founders wanted to sell snowboards online and the tools were bad.
Shopify themes are written in Liquid, a template language Shopify made and open sourced.
Webflow lets you export the HTML and CSS it generates. Clean output is the point.
A canonical tag tells search engines which URL is the real one when the same content lives at several.
A sitemap.xml lists the pages you want crawled. It is a suggestion, not a command.
A 404 means not found. A 410 means gone for good. Search engines treat them a little differently.
WCAG AA asks for 4.5 to 1 contrast on normal text. Light grey on white usually fails.
Alt text is written for screen readers first. Search engines reading it is a bonus.
A headless CMS keeps your content in an API, separate from the front end. Edit once, publish anywhere.
Lighthouse is built into Chrome DevTools. Run it before you launch, not after.
The first website went live in 1991. It was about the web itself.
Why did the developer go broke? He used up all his cache.
